title: Protected pre-change backup exists
summary: Before consequential changes, a protected backup of the affected state exists and its restore path is known.

protected.asset: Configuration, state and identity data of the deployment
protected.failure: A hardening change corrupts or locks out the deployment and no tested recovery point remains.

rationale: Every hardening change is a potential outage. A backup taken before the change, stored where the change cannot destroy it, with an owner-held recovery route outside the agent's control, converts worst-case failure into a bounded incident. A created archive is not a tested restore; the recovery route must have been exercised at least once on an isolated target.

variants.description: Use the deployment's own backup command with a scope that provably covers every change target, into protected storage.
Filesystem or volume snapshot plus a copied configuration tree, for change sets the native backup scope does not cover.

verification.method: Confirm a backup artifact exists for the change window, that its documented scope covers every planned change target, that it is stored outside the change blast radius, and that a restore has been exercised on an isolated target at least once.
verification.evidence: Backup receipt with scope and timestamp and storage location class; the isolated restore exercise record; no backup contents.

rollback.method: Not applicable: this control is itself the rollback precondition for other controls.

failure_modes: The backup scope silently omits project files or external state the change touches.
The backup is stored inside the blast radius of the change.
Restore was never exercised, so recovery is assumed rather than known.

hermes_versions.notes: Synthetic seed control: the range is an illustrative placeholder for the example registry, not a verified compatibility claim.
